questions.stem: What is the primary difference between bandwidth and throughput?

options.text: Bandwidth is the maximum data rate, while throughput is the actual data rate.
Bandwidth is measured in ms, while throughput is measured in bps.
Bandwidth is the actual data rate, while throughput is the maximum data rate.
Bandwidth and throughput are the same.

questions.explanation: Bandwidth refers to the maximum rate at which data can be transferred, while throughput is the actual rate achieved, often lower due to network conditions. Bandwidth is measured in bps, not ms.

questions.stem: Calculate the bandwidth-delay product for a network with a bandwidth of 50 Mbps and a round-trip time of 100 ms. Provide your answer in bits.
questions.explanation: Convert bandwidth to bits per second: $50 \text{ Mbps} = 50,000,000 \text{ bps}$. Convert RTT to seconds: $100 \text{ ms} = 0.1 \text{ s}$. Calculate the product: $50,000,000 \text{ bps} \times 0.1 \text{ s} = 5,000,000 \text{ bits}$.
